title: A tapejarid pterosaur from the Cambridge Greensand (Cretaceous of England), with comments on its neuroanatomy and the biogeography of the group
content:
Abstract
A reassessment of azhdarchoid pterosaur material from the Cretaceous Cambridge Greensand Member of the West Melbury Marly Chalk Formation of Great Britain is presented. The partial cranium CAMSM B54406, often referred to Ornithostoma sedgwicki, is here identified as a sinopterine tapejarid. Diagnostic traits, including the shape of the upper temporal fenestra margins and a robust, elongate supraoccipital median ridge, lead us to diagnose a new taxon, which we name Hintighernia edingerae gen. et sp. nov. Micro-CT scanning of CAMSM B54406 reveals a neuroanatomy closely resembling that of Tapejara wellnhoferi. Some additional remains from the Cambridge Greensand Member can also be referred to Tapejaridae, and we tentatively refer an isolated fragment of rostrum to cf. Hintighernia. In turn, Ornithostoma sedgwicki is regarded as a chaoyangopterid azhdarchoid, and its hypodigm is restricted to four jaw fragments. The existence of at least a third azhdarchoid species (a non-azhdarchid concilazhian) in the Cambridge Greensand is suggested based on both jaw and cervical remains. We also provide new insights regarding the biogeography of tapejarid pterosaurs. Europe appears to have been an early hotspot of phylogenetic diversity for this group and a potential point of origin for the sinopterines of Eastern Laurasia and tapejarines of South America.
